chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from more than one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who received the dowry of his daughter from her husband, then died: Is she entitled to claim her dowry from her husband, or is the father's receipt considered her receipt? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If she had authorized him to receive her dowry from her husband, she is not entitled to claim it from him; and if she had not authorized him, she is entitled to it, and the husband shall seek reimbursement from the father's heirs, unless at that time she was a minor under his guardianship, in which case it is permissible for the father to receive it on her behalf.
And if he divorces her before consummation, the father may forgive part of the dowry and take part, but he is not allowed to leave (forgive) the whole of it.
And that is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Except if they forgive or if the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives.'
Meaning the father, and the one whom the woman authorizes and entrusts her affair to, whether a brother, a relative, or someone else.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a father claiming his daughter's dowry if he received it before her death or divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the father acting as a mere agent (*wakil*) versus a guardian (*wali*) in receiving the dowry (*mahr*), determining whether the daughter retains the right to claim it directly. It further elaborates on the father's authority to forgive portions of the dowry prior to consummation, grounding this ruling in the Quranic phrase 'the one who holds the marriage contract.' This interpretation is significant in Shia fiqh for defining the economic rights of women and the paternal role in marital contracts.
